content: Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both medications. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can decrease the levels or effectiveness of demeclocycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer demeclocycline two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer doxycycline two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. The combination of didanosine and efavirenz may increase the effects of each other due to pharmacodynamic synergy. However, this increases the risk of liver toxicity. Alternative therapies should be considered. Didanosine and elivaldogene autotemcel may reduce the effects of each other. Patients should avoid taking antiretroviral medications for at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapy, during the therapy, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Close monitoring is required. Didanosine must be taken on an empty stomach. When co-administered with elvitegravir (which is taken with food), didanosine should be administered at least one hour before or two hours after elvitegravir. This combination is contraindicated. The combination of didanosine with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated because this regimen is a complete treatment for HIV and should not be combined with other antiretroviral drugs. Didanosine and ethanol may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing the risk of pancreatitis. This combination is contraindicated. Febuxostat can increase the levels or effects of didanosine by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of ferric carboxymaltose, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer the iron supplements two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Food decreases the levels of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of didanosine. Close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer fosamprenavir two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Close monitoring is required. Ganciclovir can increase the levels of didanosine by reducing renal clearance. This combination may also increase the toxicity of both drugs through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of hematologic toxicity. Alternative therapies should be considered. Didanosine can reduce the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Separate administration by 4–8 hours if necessary. The combination of didanosine and hydroxyurea increases the toxicity of both drugs through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination should be avoided due to the risk of pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy, particularly in HIV patients. Close monitoring is required. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Indinavir should be administered one hour before didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution. No significant interactions have been reported with didanosine capsules. Close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of itraconazole and ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer the antifungal agents two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Close monitoring is required. Didanosine can reduce the levels of levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, and ofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both drugs. These combinations should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer the antibiotics two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Separate administration by 4–8 hours if necessary. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of levothyroxine, liothyronine, and liotrix by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer the thyroid medications two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Close monitoring is required. Lopinavir can reduce the levels or effectiveness of didanosine by increasing gastric pH. Didanosine should be taken one hour before or two hours after lopinavir/ritonavir oral solution. This combination is contraindicated. Didanosine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period. Close monitoring is required. Didanosine can reduce the effectiveness of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. Extended-release mesalamine capsules should be administered one hour before or four hours after didanosine. Close monitoring is necessary. Methadone can reduce the levels of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of methylphenidate (specifically Ritalin LA) by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Close monitoring is required. Didanosine and metronidazole may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing the risk of peripheral neuropathy. Close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effectiveness of minocycline and tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both drugs. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer the antibiotics two hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. Close monitoring is required. Orlistat can reduce the levels or effectiveness of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if an increased viral load is confirmed. This is a partial transformation of the content provided.
